full_judgment: 60. Withholding of most relevant and vital witnesses by the prosecution compels the court to draw adverse presumption against the prosecution under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act. In good number of authorities of Apex Courts, it has been laid down, particularly in the case of State vs Sarowaruddin reported in 5 BLC 451, "The prosecution has not only with held the vital witnesses but have not also given any explanation whatsoever for their non-examination, a presumption under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act must be drawn against the prosecution for non-examination of such material and vital witnesses."
